title: Ka'ak al-Quds (Jerusalem Sesame Bread)
summary: A soft milk dough shaped into long oval rings, dipped in molasses water and sesame, baked hot and served with za'atar and olive oil.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, salt, yeast and baking powder, add the milk and oil and knead 8-10 min to a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave about 1 h until doubled. Heat the oven to 230 °C (210 °C fan).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide into 6, roll each into a 45 cm rope, join the ends and stretch into a long oval ring about 25 cm long.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Dip each ring in the molasses and water mixed together, then press both sides into the sesame.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set on the lined trays and bake 15-18 min until deep golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm, with small bowls of za'atar and olive oil for dipping.

tips: Keep the rings long and thin; they puff in the oven.
Press the sesame on firmly so it sticks.
Also good with boiled eggs and falafel.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
